short: The Globe Theatre was a prominent Elizabethan playhouse built by Shakespeare's playing company on the south bank of the Thames.
full:
Constructed in 1599 by the Lord Chamberlain's Men, the Globe Theatre was built using timber salvaged from an earlier theatre in Shoreditch. Its circular, open-air design could accommodate an audience of three thousand, varying from commoners standing in the yard to wealthy patrons paying for seated galleries under a thatched roof.

The theatre became the primary venue for many of William Shakespeare's greatest plays, embedding drama deeply into the fabric of London's cultural life. Though the original building burned down in 1613 after a stage cannon misfired during a performance, it was quickly rebuilt and remained a vital public institution until its forced closure by Parliament in 1642.
